summary_paragraph: A 59-year-old woman with HIV and end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis was admitted for shortness of breath and hypotension following an extra dialysis session. Evaluation revealed no pulmonary embolism, heart attack, or infection. The hypotension was attributed to excessive fluid removal during dialysis, and symptoms resolved with supportive care. An echocardiogram showed an atrial septal defect and mild mitral regurgitation, not requiring intervention. Workup for lymphoma was prompted by elevated LDH, thrombocytopenia, and polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia, but imaging showed no malignancy. She stabilized, continued her dialysis schedule, and was discharged home with plans to follow up on her HIV management, hematologic abnormalities, and vascular access.
problems: Herpes zoster with other nervous system complications
Kidney dialysis as the cause of abnormal reaction of patient, or of later complication, without mention of misadventure at time of procedure
